name: Sicilian Classical — Richter-Rauzer Main Line
description: The Richter-Rauzer Attack — one of the oldest and most respected anti-Sicilian weapons. After 5...Nc6, White plays 6.Bg5, pinning the Nf6 and building with Qd2 and O-O-O. Black develops naturally with ...e6, ...a6, and ...Bd7, preparing queenside counterplay with ...b5. White attacks on the kingside with pawn storms; Black races on the queenside. Opposite-side castling leads to sharp, tactical play at the highest levels.

lines.name: Classical Variation — Richter-Rauzer Main Line
lines.description: After 5...Nc6, White plays 6.Bg5 — the Richter-Rauzer Attack. The bishop pins the Nf6, pressures f6, and prepares opposite-side castling. After 7.Qd2 a6 8.O-O-O Bd7, both sides have declared their intentions: White will storm the kingside with f4-f5 and h4-h5; Black will race on the queenside with ...b5-b4. One of the oldest and most respected Sicilian systems — played from club level to world championship.
